exclusions_stated_by_publisher: Street address locations other than reported street intersections or highway locations are not exact; for victim safety they are adjusted to the nearest block level (doc_00.json description). The published address field is masked to the hundred block (e.g. '1XX DONAHUE ST', raw_cache_profile.json incident_street_address examples).
No record-level redactions or exclusions are stated in the dataset metadata (doc_00.json); the registry row lists redactions as empty (registry_row.json "redactions": "").
known_differences_from_fetch_script: Unit: one row per incident report with a single 'crime' code (unique_id distinct on all 29,701 rows; im_dr distinct on 29,700 non-null). The publisher does not say how the single code is chosen when an incident involves several offenses, so it may not follow the FBI hierarchy rule.

Aggravated assault is not mapped: 'ASSAULT' (758), 'BATTERY' (195), 'CHILD ABUS' (452) and 'CHILD NEGL' (9) all sit under crime_class 'ASSAULT - OTHER' with no aggravated/simple split, so NIBRS 13A cannot be separated from 13B.

Rape is mapped from crime 'RAPE' (crime_class 'SEXUAL ASSAULT', 29 rows) only. crime 'SEX' (353 rows, crime_class 'SEXUAL OFFENSE - OTHER') mixes other sex offenses and may hold some 11A-11C incidents; it is left unmapped, so rape undercounts (28 rows vs 50 official for 2018-2025 excluding 2021).

Larceny includes crime 'BURG AUTO' (crime_class 'BURGLARY FROM MOTOR VEHICLE'): a California vehicle burglary is theft from a motor vehicle (NIBRS 23F), not a structure burglary (220). Without it larceny would be 371 vs 548 official in 2018; with it 549 vs 548.

Motor vehicle theft uses 'VEH STLN' only; 'VEH RECV' (recovered vehicle, 312 rows) shares crime_class 'MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT' but records recoveries, and including it would give 43 vs 9 official in 2018.
FRAUD, IDENT THEF, EMBEZZLEM and FORGERY (crime_class 'FRAUD') and STOLEN PRP are not larceny under the FBI definitions and are not mapped.

Murder: the pull has one 'MURDER' row (crime_class 'HOMICIDE', 2025-01-04) while the official totals list 6 murders for 2018-2025 excluding 2021 and 0 for 2025; homicides appear to be carried under other codes (e.g. 'ADEATH', 'BODY', 'SUICIDE' death categories) that cannot be identified as 09A, so murder reconciles poorly.
Official totals for 2021 are 0 for every offense (official_totals.csv), which reads as a non-reporting year, while the pull has 3,779 rows dated 2021; 2021 will not reconcile.
notes: Publisher: Marin County Sheriff's Office (ORI CA0210000), which polices unincorporated Marin County; the only scope candidate is 06:state_nonmunicipal_remainder (scope_candidates.csv, registry_row.json), and every row has jurisdiction 'SO' (29,701 of 29,701, raw_cache_profile.json). Some rows carry points in incorporated cities or outside Marin (latitude range 35.46-44.68, longitude -124.12 to -79.96 in the pull), which the footprint and block-group join drop. Date: incident_date_time is the only published date; the documentation calls it the reported crime's 'date/time' and does not say whether it is occurrence or report time. Pull range 2018-01-01T01:59 to 2025-12-31T23:04. The where clause is the registry probe_where and matches the case text's archive filter. Coordinates: numeric latitude/longitude (26,840 non-null of 29,701), falling back to the Socrata location point, which adds 3 rows (26,843 total, computed with the runner's _coordinate on the pull); the publisher moves non-intersection addresses to the nearest block, so points are block-level approximations. Unit is incident: one row per report with one crime code; id is unique_id (distinct on every row), deduplication on it is a no-op on the archive. Offense rules map the source 'crime' codes (checked against the values in the pull): MURDER -> murder; RAPE -> rape; ROBBERY -> robbery; BURG RES, BURG COMM, BURG (crime_class BURGLARY - RESIDENTIAL/COMMERCIAL) -> burglary; THEFT, SHOPLIFTNG, BURG AUTO -> larceny; VEH STLN -> motor_vehicle_theft. Aggravated assault stays unmapped (no aggravated/simple split). Raw pull counts vs official for 2018-2025 excluding 2021, before footprint and coordinate filters (summed from per-year GROUP BY substr(incident_date_time,1,4) queries on raw_cache and from official_totals.csv): robbery 95 vs 94; larceny 3,041 vs 3,036; burglary 756 vs 686; motor vehicle theft 46 vs 34; rape 28 vs 50; murder 1 vs 6. Rows missing coordinates rise in 2022 (973) and 2023 (866) versus 75-345 in other years, which will lower located counts in those years.
